content: Swelling, redness, or pain at the site of injection may occur as a localized reaction. Nausea or diarrhea are also potential side effects of this medication. It is important to understand that this medication has been prescribed because your healthcare provider has determined that the benefits to your health outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can develop during treatment or even weeks to months after the treatment has been discontinued. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may increase the risk of developing oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection due to disruption of normal microbial flora. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare but can occur. Symptoms of a serious allergic reaction may include rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek immediate medical attention. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using ceftaroline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Additionally, ceftaroline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. It is currently unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is essential to maintain a list of all medications and supplements you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests, such as Coombs' tests or urine glucose tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While using this medication, your doctor may order laboratory tests, such as kidney function tests, to monitor your response to treatment. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not double up on doses without professional guidance. For storage, consult the product instructions or your pharmacist for specific details. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this medication. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your health needs.
